title: Are sweeteners safe and healthy
titleChinese: 甜味剂是否真的安全又健康？
paragraphs: For many of us, the relationship we have with sugar is love at first taste, and that love usually lasts a lifetime. But what price do we have to pay for this truly addictive, sugary love? Rotten teeth? Heavier bodies? Raised blood sugar levels? Or even type 2 diabetes?
Time to quit perhaps? Easier said than done. What’s the alternative? Many would suggest using sweeteners as a substitute. But are sweeteners healthier than sugar?

Sweeteners are usually low-calorie or calorie-free substances that have a similar taste to sugar. It is estimated that more than a quarter of British households buy artificial sweeteners to help cut their sugar intake.

The European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) has approved some of the health claimsfood manufacturers have made about sweeteners such as xylitol, sorbitol and sucralose. These include preventing tooth decay and controlling blood sugar levels.

According to the National Health Service in the UK, sweeteners are safe to use and are especially helpful for those who are diabetic. Sioned Quirke, a spokesperson for the British Dietetic Association says, “As a dietician, I support and promote the use of sweeteners in cooking and diet." She also says that "There is no evidence to suggest that low-calorie sweeteners, such as saccharin, aspartame and sucralose, are harmful or bad for you.”

But many have concerns over the long-term effects caused by using sweeteners. Dr Robert Lustig, author of 'Fat Chance: The Bitter Truth About Sugar' would not endorse sweeteners as an alternative to sugar because, “We have a dearth of data”. According to Dr Lustig, organisations like EFSA only require studies which test if something will poison a person in a short period of time, otherwise known as acute toxicity studies. But we still don’t know what the long-term effects are.
Dietician Emma Carder says on the NHS Choices website, “While more research is needed, sweeteners continue to have a useful role in offering a sweet taste without adding extra calories.”

sentences.english: For many of us, the relationship we have with sugar is love at first taste, and that love usually lasts a lifetime.

sentences.english: But are sweeteners healthier than sugar?
sentences.chinese: 但甜味剂比糖更健康吗？

sentences.english: Sweeteners are usually low-calorie or calorie-free substances that have a similar taste to sugar.
sentences.chinese: 甜味剂通常是低热量或无热量的物质，味道与糖相似。

sentences.english: It is estimated that more than a quarter of British households buy artificial sweeteners to help cut their sugar intake.
sentences.chinese: 据估计，超过四分之一的英国家庭购买人造甜味剂以帮助减少糖的摄入量。

sentences.english: The European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) has approved some of the health claimsfood manufacturers have made about sweeteners such as xylitol, sorbitol and sucralose.
sentences.chinese: 欧洲食品安全局（EFSA）已批准了食品制造商对木糖醇、山梨糖醇和三氯蔗糖等甜味剂做出的健康声明。

sentences.english: These include preventing tooth decay and controlling blood sugar levels.
sentences.chinese: 这些声明包括预防蛀牙和控制血糖水平。

sentences.english: According to the National Health Service in the UK, sweeteners are safe to use and are especially helpful for those who are diabetic.
sentences.chinese: 根据英国国家医疗服务体系（NHS），甜味剂可以安全使用，尤其对糖尿病患者有帮助。

sentences.english: Sioned Quirke, a spokesperson for the British Dietetic Association says, “As a dietician, I support and promote the use of sweeteners in cooking and diet."
sentences.chinese: 英国饮食协会发言人西奥内德·奎克（Sioned Quirke）说：“作为一名营养师，我支持并提倡在烹饪和饮食中使用甜味剂。”

sentences.english: She also says that "There is no evidence to suggest that low-calorie sweeteners, such as saccharin, aspartame and sucralose, are harmful or bad for you.”
sentences.chinese: 她还说：“没有证据表明低热量甜味剂，如糖精、阿斯巴甜和三氯蔗糖，对人体健康有害。”

sentences.english: But many have concerns over the long-term effects caused by using sweeteners.
sentences.chinese: 但许多人对使用甜味剂的长期影响表示担忧。

sentences.english: Dr Robert Lustig, author of 'Fat Chance: The Bitter Truth About Sugar' would not endorse sweeteners as an alternative to sugar because, “We have a dearth of data”.

sentences.english: According to Dr Lustig, organisations like EFSA only require studies which test if something will poison a person in a short period of time, otherwise known as acute toxicity studies.
sentences.chinese: 根据勒斯蒂格博士的说法，像EFSA这样的组织只要求研究某种物质是否会在短时间内毒害人体，也就是急性毒性研究。

sentences.english: But we still don’t know what the long-term effects are.
sentences.chinese: 但我们仍然不知道有什么长期影响。

sentences.english: Dietician Emma Carder says on the NHS Choices website, “While more research is needed, sweeteners continue to have a useful role in offering a sweet taste without adding extra calories.”
sentences.chinese: 营养师艾玛·卡德（Emma Carder）在NHS Choices网站上表示：“虽然需要更多的研究，但甜味剂在提供甜味而不增加额外热量方面仍然具有重要作用。”
